title: Accentuated eccentric strength training after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction during outpatient rehabilitation
summary: Patients who have undergone anterior cruciate ligament replacement surgery show strength deficits and functional movement restrictions. These problems are a result of the injury and the surgical treatment. In order to correct these deficits, multimodal therapies are carried out during prescribed rehabilitation following surgical treatment.  Various studies show that various motor deficits persist in patients who have undergone anterior cruciate ligament surgery after rehabilitation measures have been completed. In particular, there are still deficits in the area of strength, which is relevant for landing loads.  Training equipment with rotating flywheels can keep muscle tension largely constant in almost every phase of the movement cycles and can increase muscular strain, especially during the transition from eccentric to concentric work.  This accentuated eccentric training suggests a high potential for reducing muscular deficits. This study will therefore compare accentuated eccentric resistance training with standard training in a real clinical setting during outpatient rehabilitation in patients who have undergone anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction.
conditions: Patients after Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients after reconstruction of the anterior cruciate ligament,
Exclusion criteria:
there are physical limitations that do not allow the planned movement sequence (up-down movements in a two-legged stance) to be performed properly (feeling of instability) and without pain, Range of motion in the knee joint <90°, further operations planned in connection with the current indication are pending, the postoperative period is <8 weeks
